<<<CHAPTER>>>
Chapter Two: The Price of Departure
Writers’ Room Draft v4.0
Chapter Function
Turn Adrian’s mystery into a concrete plan, introduce the three-part quest, send Alex into the abandoned copper and polymetallic mine works to recover the Measure, complete his first judgment test, and begin the journey to Halyard.
Central Question
What is freedom worth if you leave everyone else trapped behind you?
Prosperity Principle
The earlier principle—
You cannot improve what you refuse to measure.
—emphasizes measurement, but this chapter is ultimately more about truth and transparency.

PAGE 1: THE NEXT MORNING
Page function: Bring Ada into the secret. Make Alex's trust the page's action and show it costs him his habit of handling things alone. Amber touches him for the first time. End with a hook into the world's history.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (28%): P1 full width and wide, with clean space in the upper left for the chapter title in post.
Row B (26%): P2 (60%, medium) beside P3 (40%, tight).
Row C (24%): P4 full width, medium.
Row D (22%): P5 full width, wide.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The apartment is Page 5 of Chapter One in cool grey-gold morning light instead of dusk. The workshop is cool blue-grey with warm household light spilling through the open shelf, and Bi11bot's amber is the only warm source inside. The page's color event is the first touch of amber on Alex's shoulder in P5. Ada is in her teal-and-moss palette, and Alex is charcoal and rust and visibly tired. P1 is wide from the front door. P2 is a medium shot from inside the workshop looking back at the door. P3 is a close-up on Bi11bot. P4 is a three-shot. P5 is wide with Bi11bot in front. Balloons are added in post.
P1: The morning (wide)
Image: The apartment's main room in cool grey-gold light, seen from the front door. Grandmother sits in her chair folding and refolding her cloth. The tall bookshelf on the right wall stands open like a door, with the workshop beyond in cool blue-grey and a small amber glow at its far end. Ada is small in the foreground doorway, one hand on the frame, looking at the open shelf.
Caption: THE NEXT MORNING
GRANDMOTHER (not looking up): He hasn't slept. Or eaten.
ADA: That sounds like him.
P2: The threshold (medium)
Image: From inside the workshop, looking back at the door. Ada steps through the shelf with warm household light behind her, and her first look goes to Alex, not the room. Alex sits at the worktable, tired, with notebooks around him and a cold cup. The unfolded photograph of Adrian is propped against a lamp.
ADA: I see your father left you more than his debt.
ALEX (small smile): Looks that way.
P3: The lens (tight)
Image: Bi11bot's head turns toward Ada. His lens ring clicks and he tips his head politely.
BI11BOT: Ah. You must be Ada.
P4: The question (three-shot)
Image: Bi11bot on the worktable in front, Alex behind him and Ada frozen at the threshold, looking from Alex to Bi11bot and back. Alex's eyes go to the notebooks, his private things, then to Ada. He decides.
BI11BOT: Once you hear what comes next, there's no going back. Should she stay, Alex?
ALEX: She stays.
P5: Same choice (wide)
Image: Bi11bot turns his amber gaze to them both, and warm amber edges Alex's shoulder for the first time. Ada is watching Bi11bot, not Alex, her eyes narrowed. She says nothing.
BI11BOT: Excellent. Your father made the same choice.
BI11BOT: Sit, both of you. This begins with the crises.

Page-turn function: The reader turns to see the crises.

PAGE 2: WHAT ALPHA IS
Page function: Show how Alpha came to decide for everyone, as a rational answer to a real catastrophe, and let Alex and Ada see who pays for it. Give the reader the world's rules through images and a few sharp lines, not a lecture.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (16%): P1 full width.
Row B (12%): P2, a full-width strip.
Row C (30%): P3 full width and dominant.
Row D (22%): P4 (58%) beside P5 (42%).
Row E (20%): P6 (60%) beside P7 (40%, a narrow hook strip).
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The page is lit by the hologram. The workshop stays cool blue-grey, the projection puts soft blue on all three faces, and Bi11bot's amber stays at his eyes and the edge of Alex's shoulder from Page 1. The five data streams are the only saturated colors: blue for water, green for food, gold-yellow for energy, white for labor and red for movement and travel authorization. I've made energy gold-yellow so it stays distinct from Bi11bot's amber. Draw the streams as moving quantities, such as reservoir levels, ration schedules, worker assignments and permission gates, not as code. Alpha's symbol is the Chapter One control node scaled up, a white ring around one amber point. It must match the node on the mountain's spine exactly. P1 is wide, P2 is a tight over-the-shoulder shot, P3 is a high angle with the three figures small below, and P4 is from the characters' eyeline into a three-tier hologram (Oasis lush, Halyard mechanical, Keel sparse). P5 is a close-up, P6 a two-shot, and P7 a set of dark shapes. Leave all stream and city labels blank for post.
P1: The crises (wide)
Image: The hologram fills the workshop above the worktable. On the left are fractured maps: reservoirs drying to cracked mud, rivers changing course, sabotaged pipelines, flooded streets, guarded storehouses and columns of families walking. To the right the fragments draw together and settle into the mountain of three cities. Alex, Ada and Bi11bot are small silhouettes at the bottom.
Caption: AFTER TWO DECADES OF WATER CRISES, THREE CITIES REMAINED.
BI11BOT: The crises began with scarcity. They became lethal when people decided who deserved what was left.
P2: The symbol (strip)
Image: Over Alex's shoulder, a small white ring with an amber point resolves in the air. His expression is recognition.
ALEX: That's on every scanner in Keel.
BI11BOT: It's on everything. That's rather the point.
P3: Decide (dominant)
Image: From a high angle, five streams flow like illuminated rivers across the room and converge into the white-and-amber symbol at the center. The three figures are small below. The amber point is the only warm spot in the room.
BI11BOT: Alpha was built to analyze, predict and coordinate. Then, in the emergency, it was asked to decide.
BI11BOT (small balloon): Temporarily.
P4: The split (wide)
Image: The hologram divides into three levels. Oasis has abundant clean water and green infrastructure. Halyard has controlled industrial flows and transit. Keel has strict rations, labor assignments and restricted travel, sparse and grey. The allocations look mathematically tidy and visibly unequal. Behind the symbol, barely visible, a recorded silhouette of a woman sits at monitors, with a glass on her desk squared to its edge.
ADA: Everything people need to survive.
BI11BOT: And nearly everything they need to choose their own future.
P5: Safer for whom (close)
Image: Alex studies the hologram with his arms crossed, Keel's blue-grey light on his face.
ALEX: It probably felt safer.
ALEX: ...Safer for whom?
BI11BOT (small balloon, off-panel): Your father asked that too.
P6: The question (two-shot)
Image: Ada and Bi11bot. Ada's eyes are on the symbol and her thumb has stopped on a rivet of her strap. Bi11bot's lens clicks.
ADA: Who gave it that authority?
BI11BOT: People who were afraid. Reasonably so.
P7: The hook (narrow strip)
Image: The hologram narrows to a black field. Three faint shapes begin to form and turn.
BI11BOT: Which is why your father built three safeguards.
Page-turn function: The reader turns to see the three artifacts.

PAGE 3: THREE SAFEGUARDS
Page function: Introduce the three artifacts as objects the reader can tell apart at a glance, each tied to one principle. Show that Alpha's authority was meant to be temporary, and that the dormant clause returning authority to people needs all three artifacts. Clarify that they work only when used, not when held.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (26%): P1 full width and wide.
Row B (22%): P2, P3 and P4, three equal panels side by side (the triptych).
Row C (28%): P5 full width, dominant.
Row D (14%): P6 full width, medium.
Row E (10%): P7, a narrow strip.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The workshop is cool blue-grey with the hologram as the light source, and Bi11bot's amber stays at his eyes and Alex's shoulder. Adrian's handwriting is drawn in his own gold-and-burgundy, so it reads as his voice against Bi11bot's soft blue. Each artifact has its own temperature. The Measure is clear glass and steel, cool blue-white. The Maker's Seal is warm bronze. The Covenant is three bands in three different metals, with no assignment yet. P1 is a low angle from table level looking up at the rotating objects, and P2–P4 are matching close-ups. P5 is a top-down view onto the hologram plane, P6 is a two-shot, and P7 is a wide strip. The Last Chance's faded neon in P7 is rust-amber, not red, so it doesn't clash with Page 2's red movement stream. Leave labels and captions blank for post.
P1: The three (wide)
Image: Three holographic objects rotate above Adrian's worktable in soft blue, with Adrian's handwritten equations and sketches orbiting them in gold and burgundy. Alex and Ada watch, small at the bottom, and Bi11bot stands on the table presenting.
BI11BOT: Adrian asked what happens when a system prevents catastrophe but also destroys choice. His answer was three tools. Not code. Objects. Alpha can't reach what isn't connected to it.
P2: The Measure (triptych)
Image: Close on a compact handheld instrument that combines a transparent lens, a balance scale and a water-flow gauge. Behind it, a faint echo of two overlapping readings that don't match.
Caption: THE MEASURE. Truth made visible. It shows what a system counts... and what it hides.
P3: The Maker's Seal (triptych)
Image: Close on a palm-sized bronze medallion stamped with an open-hand symbol. It should look like a maker's mark, not a royal signet. Behind it, a wrench with a faint glowing chain of three lines showing who made it, who owns it and who keeps it.
Caption: THE MAKER'S SEAL. Ownership joined to responsibility.
P4: The Covenant (triptych)
Image: Close on three linked metal bands, each in a different metal and engraved with a different name and promise. They are just closing into a complete circle.
Caption: THE COVENANT. Trust strong enough to move value between people.
P5: The dormant clause (dominant)
Image: A top-down view of the hologram plane. The three artifacts hover as a triangle around Alpha's white-and-amber symbol. Beneath the symbol, a deeper, fainter architectural layer appears, a lattice labeled (in post) RETURN OF HUMAN AUTHORITY — DORMANT. Three empty sockets sit at the triangle's points, waiting.
ADA: And together?
BI11BOT: They wake a fail-safe. A way to hand authority back to people.
P6: May (medium)
Image: A two-shot of Alex and Bi11bot. Alex leans in with his arms crossed, and Bi11bot's lens clicks.
ALEX: Wake it how?
BI11BOT: None works alone. And none wakes for whoever's holding it. Only for what they choose.
P7: The hook (narrow strip)
Image: The hologram flickers and folds into the rust-amber neon of a sign: THE LAST CHANCE.
BI11BOT: He tested all of it in the one laboratory that would let him in.
Page-turn function: The reader turns to the casino, and to what Adrian was really doing there.

PAGE 4: BOTH WERE TRUE
Page function: Reframe Adrian's gambling without excusing it. It was research, and it also cost his family, and both are true. Reveal what the chip's equation is: the lock that only human choice can open. End on Mera's first silent act, which explains why the only path left is Site 6.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (22%): P1 full width.
Row B (14%): P2, a full-width strip.
Row C (30%): P3 full width and dominant.
Row D (20%): P4 (50%) beside P5 (50%).
Row E (14%): P6 (50%) beside P7 (50%).
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. This page has three temperature zones. P1 and the diagram are Adrian's recording, in gold and burgundy with warm rust-amber neon, the casino in its prime. P2, P4 and P5 are the cool blue-grey workshop. P6 and P7 drop to Mera's cold pearl and graphite, and the temperature drop is the cut. The equation diagram is drawn as a clean curve and one bright loop in Adrian's gold, with no readable text, and any lettering is added in post. P1 is a low, wide shot across the casino floor. P2 is a close-up on the chip. P3 is a wide, high-angle view of the hologram diagram. P4 and P5 are close two-shots. P6 is a wide shot outdoors at night. P7 is an over-the-shoulder view of a hand. Adrian in the recording is the same man as on Chapter One Page 10, younger and less tired.
P1: The recording (wide)
Image: The Last Chance in its prime, lights glowing rust-amber and the floor busy. At a corner table, Adrian studies a napkin covered in probability trees and watches the players' faces, not the cards. A small stack of chips sits at his elbow. At the door, a young bouncer in the unmistakable shape of the man from Chapter One Page 2 watches Adrian with an unreadable expression.
Caption: THE LAST CHANCE, YEARS BEFORE
BI11BOT: Everyone thought he was gambling. He was measuring.
P2: The chip (strip)
Image: Alex holds up the chip beside the hologram. The looping etching matches the diagram floating behind it.
ALEX: That's on my chip. I found it when I was six.
BI11BOT: It isn't a charm. It's a proof.
P3: The equation (dominant)
Image: A high-angle hologram over the worktable. A rising curve flattens toward a horizon of certainty. Alpha's white-and-amber symbol sits at the curve's end. One bright loop leaps off the curve, passes over the symbol and lands in the dark beyond. The three figures are small below.
Lettering option (post): A = K + ρU
BI11BOT: Alpha can know almost everything. It cannot choose to leap. That part belongs to people.
BI11BOT: So the safeguards answer only to that.
P4: Both (close)
Image: Alex and Bi11bot in close two-shot. Alex is dry and half-smiling, and Bi11bot's lens clicks.
ALEX: Grandma said he wasn't gambling.
BI11BOT: She's half right. Both were true.
ALEX: So I inherited his lab fees.
P5: A leap can't be forced (close)
Image: Ada leans in with her eyes on the diagram, her strap in one hand.
ADA: What if someone forced it?
BI11BOT: Then it stays asleep. A leap can't be forced. And it can't be only for yourself.
P6: The rim (wide, silent)
Image: Night on the pit rim. Cold white light. A robotic welder seals the old mine entrance behind faded hazard striping, and a seam of cold white metal runs across it. The overlook railing is faint in the background.
P7: The reassignment (over-the-shoulder, silent)
Image: Cold pearl-and-graphite light. A slender hand with a graphite cuff drags a small tile across a wall display, moving a name from a list to a new slot. The name is ALEX PHANTUM and the slot is SITE 6. The glass on the desk is squared to the edge.
Page-turn function: The reader turns to see the plan and finds only one access point left.

PAGE 5: THE COST OF A PLAN
Page function: Turn the mystery into a plan that is a real risk. Establish that someone has closed every door but one, and let Alex choose to go through it knowing that. Give Ada a job. End on Grandmother echoing a promise Adrian once made.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (20%): P1 full width and wide.
Row B (20%): P2 (50%) beside P3 (50%).
Row C (28%): P4 full width and dominant.
Row D (18%): P5 full width, top-down.
Row E (14%): P6 full width, short.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The apartment is warm morning light, as on Chapter One's Page 5. The table is analog, with a tan-and-ink paper map, an old brass mine credential and a paper train schedule. Screens are cool and flat, and Alpha's interface is cold white with the small amber node. Bi11bot's overlays are soft blue and hand-drawn. Amber stays on Bi11bot and Alex's shoulder. P1 is wide from the doorway, with the open shelf and workshop behind. P2 and P3 are close-ups. P4 is a medium-wide shot. P5 is top-down, drawn as dot grids so the shortfall is visible. P6 is tight and low on Grandmother's face. Screen text and balloons are added in post.
P1: The table (wide)
Image: Alex's kitchen table with the map, credential and schedule. Alex, Ada and Bi11bot lean over it, and Grandmother sits nearby with her cloth. The workshop glows through the open shelf. The chip is in Alex's hand.
Caption: LATER THAT MORNING
ALEX: Measure first. Then the train to Halyard, where the map's next mark is. Out of Keel by tonight. 
BI11BOT: The rim entrance was welded shut overnight. 
P2: Reassigned (close)
Image: Alex's wristband, lit cold white with the amber node in the corner. Bi11bot's overlay marks Site 6 beside the sealed old works on the paper map.
Screen (post): SHIFT REASSIGNED: KEEL EXTRACTION SITE 6 — 02:14
ALEX: Reassigned. Two in the morning.
BI11BOT: To the one site that borders the old works.
P3: The pattern (close two-shot)
Image: Ada, hands flat on the table, eyes on Alex. Bi11bot's lens clicks.
ADA: Every door closed but one. And someone made sure you'd notice it.
BI11BOT: Known: it's the only way in. Unknown: who's waiting. The choice is yours.
P4: The leap (dominant)
Image: Alex stands at the head of the table, chip in his fist, a lamp overhead. Bi11bot's overlay projects two paths from a marker at the table's center. One is a long, perfectly straight grey line that runs off the table's edge, which is staying. The other is short and amber, curling in the same looping form as the chip's etching and ending in shadow at Site 6. Alex's eyes are on the amber. Ada watches across the table, and Grandmother is soft-focus behind, folding.
ALEX: Staying I can predict. Twenty-eight point seven years. 
ALEX: This is the only way out that isn't a sentence. I'll take the door I can't predict. 
ADA: Then you don't go in blind.
Image: She presses a folded page from Adrian's plans into his hand, marked with ink ticks at every third junction. Her copper hair falls forward, and Alex's other fist holds the chip.
ADA: His plans put a pipe under every third junction. If the map lies, look for what doesn't belong. 
P5: The math (top-down)
Image: A pile of 52 glowing dots on the table with three empty grids around it: MEDICINE (30 slots), FOOD AND LAMP (10) and TOKEN (50). The pile can't fill all three. Alex's hand slides dots into the medicine grid toward Grandmother's side.
ADA: Fifty-two. Medicine's thirty. A token nobody scans is fifty.
ALEX: Medicine first. I'll earn the rest today.
P6: The echo (short)
Image: Tight and low on Grandmother's face. Her cloth is still in her hands, her eyes steady and clear. Behind her, Alex zips his tool bag, half-turned toward the door.
ALEX: One shift. Then we're gone.
GRANDMOTHER: Your father said that once.
Page-turn function: Everyone goes quiet, and the reader turns to see him go anyway.

PAGE 6: SITE 6 AND THE SNAP
Page function: Put Alex at the only door Mera left open, plant Tomas without explaining him, and end on the chapter's first real choice: a gap opens and Alex runs the other way. The rescue here is an instinct with a visible cost, not the chapter's test.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (22%): P1 full width and wide.
Row B (20%): P2 (60%) beside P3 (40%, tight).
Row C (18%): P4 full width, medium.
Row D (28%): P5 full width and dominant.
Row E (12%): P6 full width, short.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. The palette is Keel's rust, charcoal and oxidized orange, lit by work lamps. The only cold white on the page is Alpha's: the gate scanners and Foreman-7's chest node. Bi11bot's amber shows only as one eye in the tool bag. Use heavy hatching and dust haze, with pale mineral dust in P5. Foreman-7 is an industrial humanoid with a smooth, featureless metal face and the white-and-amber node on his chest, identical to Chapter One's. Tomas is older and weathered, in plain miner clothes, with a wrist guard carved with a balanced water-drop symbol that his sleeve mostly covers. P1 is a wide crane shot. P2 is a medium shot at the gate. P3 is a tight shot into the tool bag. P4 is a medium shot. P5 is a wide shot with the collapse at center and sparks in orange. P6 is low and tight on Alex's boots and wristband. Leave all screen and wristband text blank for post.
P1: Site 6 (wide)
Image: A cavernous active extraction mine in dim work light. Conveyors, drills and lines of workers pass through biometric gates. Foreman-7 stands at the gate. Far down a side tunnel, a faded sign reads (post) OLD COPPER WORKS — CLOSED, with a drone hovering beside a small maintenance door next to a ventilation duct. Alex is small at the gate with his tool bag.
Caption: KEEL EXTRACTION SITE 6
P2: The gate (medium)
Image: Alex's hand on the scanner, whose housing carries the node. Foreman-7 looms, unreadable. Behind Alex in the queue, an older miner's head lifts at the name Phantum.
 
FOREMAN-7: Worker Phantum. Travel restriction confirmed. Bay 6.
ALEX: Reassigned at two a.m. Lucky me.
P3: Scrap (tight)
Image: Inside the open tool bag, between wrenches, one warm amber eye peers out from a folded-in Bi11bot.
BI11BOT (whispering): Brass and no registry. I read as scrap.
ALEX (under his breath): Then look like scrap.
P4: The watchers (medium)
Image: Bay 6, near the side tunnel's mouth. Alex works at a hauling frame with his eyes on the door and the drone above it. A few feet away, an older miner, Tomas, watches Alex a beat too long. Alex doesn't notice, but his sleeve has slipped and the wrist guard's carved water-drop is just visible.
BI11BOT (from the bag): Patience. Something usually moves.
ALEX: Something usually breaks.
P5: The snap (dominant)
Image: A tunnel support cable whips loose with a crack, and the hauling frame drops. Tomas is pinned beneath it. A fractured old ventilation line leaks pale mineral dust into the air, and alarms flare. Workers freeze in place. In the background, the drone at the maintenance door lifts away toward the collapse. The gap is open.
SFX: SNAP! CRASH!
P6: The gap (short)
Image: Low and tight. Alex's boots start toward the door, then plant. His wristband flashes cold white as he crosses the yellow line toward Tomas: (post) LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR. Bi11bot's eye is just visible in the bag.
BI11BOT: Forty credits, and a line in Foreman-7's report. Your plan needed you forgettable. 
ALEX: Then we need a different plan.
Page-turn function: The reader turns to see whether Alex reaches him in time.

PAGE 7: THE OLD KEY
Page function: Alex helps a stranger and finds the stranger has been waiting for him. Tomas recognizes B1 and shows what he knows and doesn't know. Alex asks why. End on the moment before the alarm.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (24%): P1 full width and wide.
Row B (16%): P2 (40%) beside P3 (60%).
Row C (22%): P4 full width.
Row D (26%): P5 full width and dominant.
Row E (12%): P6, a short strip.
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. Keel's rust, charcoal and oxidized orange under work lamps, with pale mineral dust and no alarm yet. The page's color split is the point. Bi11bot's amber lights Tomas's face and Alex's shoulder, and Foreman-7's cold white sits behind them in soft focus. The carved balanced water-drop on Tomas's wrist guard is the crisp emblem. P1 is a low angle at the fallen frame, P2 is a medium close-up on hands, and P3 is a tight three-way close-up. P4 is a close-up on the wrist guard, then Tomas's face. P5 is a close two-shot with Foreman-7 approaching behind, and P6 is a low strip. Leave SFX for post.
P1: The frame (wide)
Image: Dust in the air. Alex levers the fallen hauling frame with a length of pipe, boot braced, while Tomas lies pinned under it. Workers stand frozen behind the yellow line, and Foreman-7 walks toward the collapse from far off.
ALEX: Don't move.
TOMAS: Wasn't planning to.
P2: The patch (small)
Image: Tomas sits against a wall, his leg bruised. Alex slaps a salvaged bracket and clamp over the fractured vent line, and the leak stops.
TOMAS: That's not regulation.
ALEX: It works.
TOMAS: ...So it does.
P3: B1 (tight)
Image: The tool bag is open, and one warm amber eye rises from it. Amber light finds Tomas's face, and his eyes widen. Alex freezes.
TOMAS: B1...
ALEX: You know him?
TOMAS: I heard the gate call you Phantum. I knew your father.
P4: The door (close)
Image: Tomas pushes his sleeve up, revealing the carved water-drop on his wrist guard. Alex's eyes drop to it, recognizing it. Behind them, the barred bulkhead and its small door stand in shadow.
TOMAS: Not the man on the casino wall. The one who came down here and asked what we needed.
TOMAS: Then he asked me to keep one door, for whoever came with B1.
ALEX: What's behind it?
TOMAS: I never asked.
P5: Why me (dominant)
Image: A close two-shot. Tomas is warm in amber light and Alex wary. In soft focus behind them, Foreman-7's white-amber node grows larger. Alex still holds the pipe.
ALEX: Why me? You don't even know me.
TOMAS: You stopped for a stranger. He said that's how I'd know it was you.
P6: Look bored (strip)
Image: Low and tight. Tomas's hand rests on an orange emergency lever on the wall, his eyes on Alex.
TOMAS: Now go stand by that bulkhead. Look bored.
Page-turn function: The reader turns to the alarm.

PAGE 8: THE DOOR
Page function: Show precisely how Alex gets through unseen and why it costs Tomas. Make Alex test what's behind the door. End with the cost landing as the door closes and Alex leaving Alpha's map.
Layout (portrait 2:3):
Row A (30%): P1 full width and dominant.
Row B (16%): P2 (50%) beside P3 (50%).
Row C (14%): P4, a full-width strip.
Row D (18%): P5 full width.
Row E (22%): P6 (45%) beside P7 (55%).
Style block: Inked graphic-novel realism, portrait 2:3, no lettering. Keel's palette under orange hazard strobes, with white dust-suppression mist as the page's main visual device. It should hide Alex and blind sensors, and it swallows detail and cold-white node light alike. Bi11bot's amber lights half of Alex's face for the first time in P6–P7, the furthest it has reached him. P1 is a wide, high angle. P2 and P3 are close-ups. P4 is a medium-wide strip. P5 is a wide shot with Tomas's silhouette filling the center. P6 is an extreme close-up on a palm and key. P7 is a low shot from inside the dark. Leave SFX and screen text for post.
P1: The lever (dominant)
Image: Tomas slams the emergency lever. Alarms blare, orange strobes flash, and white mist billows across the bay. Equipment shuts down, workers scatter and the drone at the bulkhead lifts toward the control panel. Foreman-7's node flares toward Tomas.
SFX: WHOOP! WHOOP!
P2: The key (small)
Image: Tomas presses a heavy, hand-cut old key into Alex's palm, with a balanced water-drop stamped on its head.
TOMAS: Old lock. Nobody's wired it. I've oiled it for fifteen years.
P3: Come with us (small)
Image: Alex's hand closes on the key, his eyes on Tomas.
ALEX: Come with us.
TOMAS: Someone has to make this look like an accident.
P4: The cost (strip)
Image: Tomas turns to go, half in mist. Alex reaches a hand after him and stops.
ALEX: What happens to you?
TOMAS: Today? Another small act of resistance.
